clue.text: One needed at first in case of break?

definitions.text: One needed at first in case of break?

indicators.note: a case holds something, so the word for break is the casing round the other piece

parts.note: to split is to break apart

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word needed

explanation.surface: A question about what you would want first when a bone is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a support strapped on is what a broken limb needs at first. 'At first' gives N, and 'in case of' puts N inside SPLIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigid support bound to a fractured limb is the first-aid item needed when a bone breaks.

clue.text: Delicious exercise — painful afterwards

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
achy means sore or painful

explanation.surface: A workout that tastes good but leaves you hurting afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Afterwards' simply orders the charade: the painful part comes second. PE is physical education, a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something excellent or lovely is described as peachy, a synonym for delicious.

clue.text: Unabridged big band music well under way

parts.note: an unabridged text is given in full
swing is the jazz style of the big bands

explanation.surface: An uncut recording of big band jazz playing at its height.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: an activity at its liveliest, fully active, is described as being at the peak of its swing.

clue.text: Merit rest, struggling for a third of one's pregnancy

indicators.note: struggling suggests the words merit rest thrash about into a new order

explanation.surface: A pregnant woman deserving a break while she struggles through part of her term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges MERITREST.
explanation.definitionFit: Pregnancy is divided into three periods of about three months, each called by this term.

clue.text: Devil's Island?

parts.note: read not as the French penal colony but as the island home of a famous marsupial devil

explanation.surface: Asking about the notorious French penal colony off South America.
explanation.walkthrough: Devil's Island was a French prison colony; here the devil is the Tasmanian devil, a carnivorous marsupial, so its island is the Australian state.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian island state is the only wild home of the marsupial known as the devil.

clue.text: Culture budget finally supported by suit

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of, supported by, the next
finally takes the closing letter of budget

parts.note: hearts is one of the four suits of cards

explanation.surface: Funding for culture finally being backed by a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supported by' puts T above HEARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Music, painting, theatre and literature together are referred to collectively as culture.

clue.text: Rising talents, something to hang on to

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: parts, as in a man of many parts, are talents

explanation.surface: Up-and-coming talents being given something to cling to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns PARTS upwards into the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop of leather or fabric held by standing passengers on a bus is something to grip.

clue.text: Start to change right down in vehicle for curve

indicators.note: the first letter is to shift all the way down to the bottom of the down entry

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Instructions for a vehicle to change down a gear and turn right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to change right down' moves the C of CAR to the bottom, giving ARC. 'Change down' pretends to be about gears.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment of a circle's circumference is a curved line, so a curve.

clue.text: Send down troublemaker? Definitely not up!

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous troublemaker

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the phrase reads from bottom to top

parts.note: no sir is an emphatic refusal

explanation.surface: Sending a troublemaker down from school, never promoting him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses NOSIR to RISON beneath IMP. 'Send down' is British for expelling from university, but here it means jailing.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge who sends a criminal down is committing them to jail, so locking them up.

clue.text: Property of some elements: not all lithium and iron

parts.note: half is not all of something
Li is the chemical symbol for lithium
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A chemistry note on lithium and iron, which only partly share a property.
explanation.definitionFit: Radioactive elements have a characteristic time for half their atoms to decay, a measurable property.

clue.text: Ready to accept extremely eccentric instructions

indicators.note: ripe takes in the other letters, accepting them inside

parts.note: ripe fruit is ready to eat

indicators.note: extremely takes the outermost letters of eccentric

explanation.surface: Someone happy to take on odd instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready to accept' reads like a willing person, but 'Ready' is the outer word and 'to accept' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook follows a set of directions for making a dish, so these are instructions.

clue.text: Not now handle short planks

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: shelves are planks fixed to a wall

explanation.surface: Putting off dealing with some short planks of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the S from SHELVES. The definition reads as a verb phrase: handle later, not now.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone dealing with a matter is to put it aside to handle at a later time.

clue.text: Country inn, smashing treasure from the past

indicators.note: the inn smashes into the relic, ending up inside it

parts.note: a relic is a treasured object surviving from the past
a pub is an inn

explanation.surface: A country inn, wonderful, filled with treasures from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country inn' reads as one phrase and 'smashing' as British for wonderful; in fact 'Country' is the definition and 'smashing' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A state governed by elected representatives without a monarch is a type of nation.

clue.text: Take one's peck of dirt, and die?

definitions.meaning: literally, to bite a mouthful of soil
slang for being killed or failing

explanation.surface: Asking whether eating a portion of dirt might be fatal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everyone must eat a peck of dirt before he dies' is an old proverb; a peck is a dry measure.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for falling dead, originally of a fallen warrior's face in the ground.

clue.text: Pleasure of relation stopping at party

indicators.note: the word at plugs, stops up, the word for relation

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a relation
a faction is a party within a group

explanation.surface: A relative enjoying stopping off at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping' means plugging, as a stopper fills a bottle, so it signals one piece set inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Contentment from a need met is pleasure, a close synonym.

clue.text: An old idea re-expressed in such an affected voice

definitions.note: the adjective describes a voice of this kind

indicators.note: the words an old idea are expressed again in a new order

explanation.surface: An old idea restated in a nasal, affected way.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-expressed' rearranges ANOLDIDEA. The definition describes the kind of voice, so it answers to an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A nasal voice sounding as if the nose were blocked by swollen tissue is described by this adjective.

clue.text: One made fun of in proper reply to accusation

indicators.note: the word for the mocked one goes inside the word for proper

parts.note: real means proper, genuine
a butt is the target of jokes

explanation.surface: Someone mocked giving a proper reply to an accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One made fun of' is the butt of a joke; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A counter-argument or contradiction of a charge is a reply to it.

clue.text: Mentions more need to revise, having memory lapse

indicators.note: the words mentions more need revising, so are rearranged

explanation.surface: Notes that need revising because someone has had a forgetful moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need to revise' rearranges MENTIONSMORE.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal term for a momentary forgetfulness blamed on getting older.

clue.text: Sharp point seized in fighting over transport

indicators.note: the sharp point is gripped inside the fighting word
in a down entry over means the word is turned upwards

parts.note: sumo is Japanese wrestling, a form of fighting
a nib is the sharp point of a pen

explanation.surface: A sharp point caught in a scuffle on public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the wrestling word upwards in this down entry, giving OMUS, before 'seized in' closes it round the point.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus, from the Latin for 'for all', is a means of public transport.

clue.text: Take over second source of gold

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second
gold is mined from a vein in rock

explanation.surface: Taking over a second gold mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang on a mo' is British for 'wait a second'.
explanation.definitionFit: To occupy a new home or territory is to take it over.

clue.text: My better weapon, notice, tossed in the drink

parts.note: a gun is a weapon

indicators.note: the notice is thrown into the drink, inside it

parts.note: gin is a drink
an ad is a notice

explanation.surface: A weapon and a notice thrown into the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's poem ends 'You're a better man than I am, Gunga Din', so the water-carrier is the speaker's better; 'tossed in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's water-carrier is called a better man by the poem's speaker, so he is that speaker's better.

clue.text: Run in late, in fear

indicators.note: the run goes inside the word for late

parts.note: the late person is dead
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Arriving late in a state of fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside DEAD. 'Late' means deceased, as in 'the late king'.
explanation.definitionFit: Great fear or apprehension is a synonym of the noun.

clue.text: King gives medal to president

parts.note: an OBE is a British honour with a medal, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
Ron Reagan was a US president

explanation.surface: A king awarding a medal to a president.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's king of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: It holds fast food

definitions.meaning: a wire fastener that keeps papers together
a basic foodstuff such as rice or bread

explanation.surface: Something that keeps fast food in its wrapper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast food' is a false compound: the clue splits after 'fast'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent wire fixes papers together; a staple diet is basic food.

clue.text: Secretary's first to open one letter, then another

indicators.note: the first letter opens up the Greek letter, getting inside it

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of secretary

explanation.surface: A secretary first opening one letter and then another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives S, which 'to open' puts inside PI. The definition is 'another' Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenty-third letter of the Greek alphabet is another letter after pi.

clue.text: Covered with splashes of gold in twin room?

indicators.note: the gold sits inside the twin rooms
twin means the room word appears twice side by side

parts.note: bed is short for bedroom
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A twin room covered in splashes of gold paint.
explanation.walkthrough: A twin room has two beds, which is why 'twin' doubles the room word.
explanation.definitionFit: To smear something with paint or mud is to daub it thoroughly, leaving it covered.

clue.text: Strangely pleased with one group of sisters

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of pleased with one sit oddly, rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A group of sisters oddly delighted with one thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' rearranges PLEASED plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the seven daughters of Atlas, later a star cluster, are a group of sisters.

clue.text: Put match to some list of complaints

parts.note: to put a match to something is to light it, past tense lit
any means some

explanation.surface: Setting fire to part of a list of grievances.
explanation.definitionFit: A long tedious recital of grievances, by extension from a series of prayers.
